Cleavable + rigid requests return a two-part composite construct (rigid spacer + flexible GS-flanked protease cassette) because proteolysis requires local backbone unfolding (Hubbard et al. 1994).
Mined candidates (`mined_high_confidence_dfl_call`) are model-called inter-domain spans from Part 1 and carry explicit provenance flags distinct from curated natural or literature authorities.

citations.ca_virtual_bond: van Rosmalen, M., Krom, M., & Merkx, M. (2017). Tuning the flexibility of glycine-serine linkers to allow rational design of multidomain proteins. Biochemistry, 56(50), 6565-6574. https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.biochem.7b00902 - contour length per residue b0 = 3.8 A.
citations.disulfide_criteria: Sowdhamini, R., Srinivasan, N., Shoichet, B., Santi, D. V., Ramakrishnan, C., & Balaram, P. (1989). Stereochemical modeling of disulfide bridges: criteria for introduction into proteins by site-directed mutagenesis. Protein Engineering, 3(2), 95-103. https://doi.org/10.1093/protein/3.2.95 - candidate pairs have Ca-Ca distance no more than 6.5 A and Cb-Cb no more than 4.5 A. The lower end of the Ca-Ca window used here is a steric floor set to one virtual Ca-Ca bond, not a published criterion.
citations.extended_rise: Pauling, L., & Corey, R. B. (1951). The pleated sheet, a new layer configuration of polypeptide chains. PNAS, 37(5), 251-256. https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.37.5.251 - axial translation per residue in the pleated sheet, 3.3-3.5 A, i.e. the realistic fully extended rise; the 3.8 A virtual bond is the absolute trans-peptide ceiling.
citations.gs_chain_statistics: van Rosmalen, M., Krom, M., & Merkx, M. (2017), Table 1 and eq 7 - persistence lengths and characteristic ratios C_inf for GS-rich linkers, and the Gaussian-chain relation <re^2> = C_inf * n * b0^2.
citations.helical_linker_design: Arai, R., Ueda, H., Kitayama, A., Kamiya, N., & Nagamune, T. (2001). Design of the linkers which effectively separate domains of a bifunctional fusion protein. Protein Engineering, 14(8), 529-532. https://doi.org/10.1093/protein/14.8.529 - A(EAAAK)nA linkers form alpha-helices and separate domains by an amount that grows with n; the paper reports CD/FRET trends, not a per-residue rise, so the rise above is used.
citations.helix_rise: Pauling, L., Corey, R. B., & Branson, H. R. (1951). The structure of proteins: two hydrogen-bonded helical configurations of the polypeptide chain. PNAS, 37(4), 205-211. https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.37.4.205 - alpha-helix translation per residue 1.47-1.5 A along the helix axis.
citations.interdomain_linker_lengths: George, R. A., & Heringa, J. (2002). An analysis of protein domain linkers: their classification and role in protein folding. Protein Engineering, 15(11), 871-879. https://doi.org/10.1093/protein/15.11.871 - natural interdomain linker length distribution, used only as context for reporting, never as a threshold.
citations.max_asa: Tien, M. Z., Meyer, A. G., Sydykova, D. K., Spielman, S. J., & Wilke, C. O. (2013). Maximum allowed solvent accessibilites of residues in proteins. PLoS ONE, 8(11), e80635. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0080635 - theoretical MaxASA values used to normalise ASA into relative solvent accessibility.
citations.rsa_threshold: Rost, B., & Sander, C. (1994). Conservation and prediction of solvent accessibility in protein families. Proteins, 20(3), 216-226. https://doi.org/10.1002/prot.340200303 - the buried/exposed relative-accessibility convention. Published cutoffs range from about 5% to 25%; LinkerForge reports the value and all three bands rather than picking one.
citations.sasa_algorithm: Shrake, A., & Rupley, J. A. (1973). Environment and exposure to solvent of protein atoms. Lysozyme and insulin. Journal of Molecular Biology, 79(2), 351-371. https://doi.org/10.1016/0022-2836(73)90011-9 - numerical sphere-point solvent accessible surface area with a 1.4 A water probe.
citations.sasa_definition: Lee, B., & Richards, F. M. (1971). The interpretation of protein structures: estimation of static accessibility. Journal of Molecular Biology, 55(3), 379-400. https://doi.org/10.1016/0022-2836(71)90324-X - definition of solvent accessible surface area and the 1.4 A probe radius.
citations.vdw_radii: Bondi, A. (1964). van der Waals volumes and radii. The Journal of Physical Chemistry, 68(3), 441-451. https://doi.org/10.1021/j100785a001
citations.wlc: Kratky, O., & Porod, G. (1949). Rontgenuntersuchung geloster Fadenmolekule. Recueil des Travaux Chimiques des Pays-Bas, 68(12), 1106-1122. https://doi.org/10.1002/recl.19490681203 - worm-like chain mean square end-to-end distance used with the persistence lengths above.

out_of_scope: Expression, folding and activity of the resulting construct.
Whether the two domains disrupt each other's structure or interact at a new interface.
Linker sequence choice beyond the flexible/helical distinction.
Conformational ensembles: only one input conformation is measured.
